title: Unlock your creativity
lede: Michael teaches at Art Junction — in the studio, online and one-to-one — for complete beginners and experienced artists alike. Topics include drawing with charcoal, fabricating steel and casting in bronze.
intro:
Michael's teaching looks beyond the representational, into the imaginative recesses of the creative mind. He encourages the brave steps and artistic risks that unlock creativity, and the confidence to take on fresh subjects: sounds, feelings, emotions or actions.

Equally at home drawing, painting or sculpting, he moves freely between 2D and 3D. Whatever your level, he will look at and discuss your work in a respectful, helpful and constructively critical way.

offers.title: In-studio workshops
offers.detail: Two-day courses at the Art Junction studio
offers.text: Hands-on courses at the Art Junction studio, with materials included and a small group, so everyone gets time with Michael. They have included Making a Self Portrait and a five-day course, Creating Abstract Sculpture in Jesmonite. Current dates are listed above.

offers.title: One-to-one sessions
offers.text: Bring your own work for a focused conversation about where it could go next — technique, composition and finding your own voice.

offers.title: Livestream life sessions
offers.text: For anyone who wants to move beyond copying what is in front of them: ideas, methods and techniques to see differently and draw more expressively.

offers.title: How-to videos & guides
offers.text: Short films and articles on drawing with charcoal, animal subjects, fabricating steel structures, casting in bronze (and how to save money doing so), and a personal overview of the creative process.

quote: Being a tutor is not about me or my work. It's about bringing the best out of other people — helping them to progress, helping them to achieve.

testimonials.text: Michael comes from a completely different viewpoint — questioning can be challenging at first, but Michael always has an answer and you come away with a much broader perspective on what is possible.

Michael seems to work a bit like a grasshopper! He has the unusual ability to move from 2D to 3D, from drawing to a pair of scissors, from cardboard cut-out to bronze sculpture. It's a bit like having Picasso on Blue Peter.

Michael gives a contemporary expression to the ideals of Paul Nash, Eric Ravilious and other British artists in the early 20th century who produced designs and illustrations commercially alongside their output of fine art.
